- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If supply net is heavily negative (e.g., -15+), model underestimates price; add 3–8% to forecast mean to reflect supply tightness.
- When bullish sentiment is low (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model often underreacts — increase forecast baseline by 5–10% to capture hidden demand.
- If sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust — apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecast mean to reflect sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from model, check if recent auction supply events occurred — if yes, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for supply shock.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., -0.5 to -1.0) and model ignores them, apply a 3–7% downward bias to forecast mean to reflect sentiment lag.
